I farm 24 mu, and because I have well irrigation and long experience with the wheat-maize system, I will keep that as the backbone of my land use this year. I do not want to spread myself too thin with only two people in the household and some labor going off-farm, so I will keep most of the land in the wheat-maize rotation and leave a smaller share for cotton. I will put 18 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same fields, and 6 mu into cotton. For wheat, I will use improved seed, give enough nitrogen for steady tillering and grain filling, add phosphorus and some potassium, irrigate a few times because I have well water, and keep tillage simple with rotary work so I can manage labor and costs. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I care about stable yield, keep fertilizer at a moderate-to-strong level after wheat, irrigate when needed in summer, and use fewer pesticide sprays unless pressure rises. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area because it takes more hands and attention, but I will still plant it for income balance; I will use improved seed, fertilize moderately, irrigate several times from the well, and expect more pesticide work than for grain crops. My choices are based on what I can manage myself, the crops I already know well, and the fact that I have irrigation but limited household labor.
